notes: SHIP v1.14.395 - M0: BUILD THE INSTRUMENT BEFORE CHANGING THE THING IT MEASURES. First ship of the approved ARCHITECTURE BLUEPRINT program. Zero visual change, zero behaviour change except honesty. Nothing in the rack scene, the renderer lifecycle, or any user-facing surface moves here - that is deliberate. The owner asked for renderer counts BEFORE and AFTER the correction, and those numbers are only comparable if they come from the same instrument, so the instrument ships first. THREE ITEMS. (1) NON-ALLOCATING WebGL OBSERVER - new PhantomGL object answers the owner's 15 runtime questions on hardware: canvas total / visible / hidden, live vs lost vs refused contexts, the rack and aisle mount owners, three.js state, boot-loop state. THE HARD RULE IS THAT IT MUST NEVER CAUSE A CONTEXT TO EXIST. getContext() is only a READ on a canvas that already holds that context; on a bare canvas it CREATES one. So context state is read back ONLY from the mounts the app already tracks (_reh3dActive / _forge3dActive), which are known to hold contexts, and every other canvas is counted and reported as 'unprobed' - an honest gap rather than a silent allocation. An earlier draft of this observer scanned every canvas in the DOM and would have reproduced the exact bug it exists to detect; it was caught before it was written. (2) THE CAPABILITY PROBES STOP LEAKING CONTEXTS - reh3d_webglOK() and bw_mount3D's diag() each minted a fresh canvas and took a REAL WebGL context that was never released. reh3d_webglOK ran on every rack-detail open and every Forge close. diag() ran on the FAILURE path, which means it asked the browser for another context at the exact moment the app was out of them. It is also why the device reported 'WebGL support: true' in the same breath as 'context REFUSED' - that 'true' came from a different, freshly minted canvas, not from the rack canvas. The two statements were never in conflict; the diagnostic was measuring the wrong object. Capability is now probed at most ONCE per session, the probe slot is handed straight back via WEBGL_lose_context, and the answer is cached on the function object. diag() additionally now reports rackCtx - the actual state of THIS mount's canvas - which is the question that was always being asked. (3) THE TWO BOOT ANIMATION LOOPS ARE CANCELLED - the void-motes loop and the code-streaming eyes loop each ran with no exit condition, no stored handle and no visibility guard. launch() only sets boot.style.display='none' (boot.remove() appears nowhere in the file), so both closures held live canvas references and both loops ran at full rate for the entire shift on the primary device. They are 2D contexts, so they are NOT the cause of the WebGL refusal - but they are a continuous GPU/CPU tax and a plausible aggravator, since iOS WebKit sheds WebGL contexts under memory pressure. Both now record their rAF handle and are cancelled in launch(). GATES: 3 inline script blocks compile clean x3, CSS braces balanced 4557/4557, line endings preserved (repo is LF end-to-end; HEAD blob 54045 bare LF, working copy 54173 = 54045 + 137 - 9), diff confined to dct-ios.html. NOT IN THIS SHIP AND DELIBERATELY SO: the RackExperience controller, the reclaim barrier, scene reuse, and every routing / storage / composition change. DEVICE-VERIFY: cold load, open Build, and read the diagnostic line if the rack fails - it now names rackCtx and a live canvas census. Rack behaviour is unchanged from .394; if it drew before it draws now, and if it refused before it still refuses. What changes is that the refusal is now measured correctly.
